item.title: Flydubai saga captures Israel’s role in a new Middle East - and its old limits
item.description: DIPLOMATIC AFFAIRS: From Netanyahu’s UAE visit to the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, a dramatic week reveals the possibilities and limits of regional cooperation.

item.title: Farewell from the Report: reflecting on three years of upheaval - from the editor
item.description: On the third anniversary of October 7, Editor-in-Chief, Ruth Marks Eglash reflects on a year at The Jerusalem Report and bids readers farewell

item.title: El Al forced to cancel first rescue flights to Dubai after authorities revoke landing permissions
item.description: El Al stated that, as soon as official permission is granted for the rescue flights to resume, it would be implementing the planned flights to bring stranded Israelis home.

item.title: Omani flydubai hijacking suspect held no second nationality, sources say – exclusive
item.description: Sources with knowledge of the investigation also disputed claims that the Israel-UAE aviation agreement limits pilots to nationals of countries with diplomatic ties to Israel.

item.title: 'The cockpit was empty': Israeli recounts fight to survive flydubai attempted hijacking - exclusive
item.description: At a beachfront hotel in Tel Aviv, Tal reconstructs the moment he had to get two additional pilots to the controls, the efforts to secure the aircraft and the moment he thought about his children.

item.title: Flydubai hijacking: Israel is a nation of heroes - time for the gov't to show courage too - opinion
item.description: We have now heard some testimony from passengers aboard the flight. It is frightening and disturbing, particularly as investigators are still trying to understand what exactly happened.

item.title: Mamdani calls Netanyahu 'architect of horrific genocide,' calls for US to join ICC, enforce warrant
item.description: Mamdani made the remarks in an extensive interview on the American podcast This Past Weekend, hosted by Theo Von, a well known comedian and podcaster who regularly interviews public figures.

item.title: Herzog visits elderly Arab man attacked at Damascus gate, expresses sympathy, support
item.description: Herzog told Ahmed al-Husseini, 66, that he was "truly saddened to see what happened to you, and I think the entire people of Israel was deeply pained to see this incident."

item.title: Iran weighing options against US, Israel as nuclear talks stall, Israeli defense official says
item.description: A senior Israeli defense official said Iran's room for maneuver has narrowed amid US sanctions, while Israel is preparing for the possibility that an Iranian move could spiral out of control.

item.title: Who will teach the next generation?
item.description: A Jerusalem summit will bring together more than 300 educators from Israel and around the world to share ideas, confront common challenges, and strengthen the connections that sustain Jewish life.

item.title: No. 1: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump: Remembering who brought the hostages home
item.description: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump helped achieve what few in Jerusalem thought possible, bringing every Israeli hostage home and reshaping the Middle East.

item.title: No. 3: Gadi Eisenkot: Israel’s next prime minister?
item.description: The former IDF chief has emerged as the leading opposition challenger to Netanyahu, offering voters a path to a post-Netanyahu Israel.

item.title: No. 4: Naftali Bennett: The former PM seeking a comeback to ‘repair Israel’
item.description: Since returning to politics, Bennett has shifted from his previous campaigns, taking a more liberal position while maintaining a strong right-wing stance on security.

item.title: No. 5: Ronald Lauder: Standing at the forefront of the fight against antisemitism
item.description: Lauder has never confined himself to quiet philanthropy - he continues to use his position to demand accountability from political leaders.

item.title: No. 2: Benjamin Netanyahu: Shaping Israel’s politics and global image for a generation
item.description: Netanyahu has become more than Israel’s prime minister for many. Abroad, for instance, he has become Israel’s symbol and the lightning rod for much of the hatred directed against the Jewish state.

item.title: Ambassador to UAE says flydubai incident didn't weaken Israel-Emirati relations - interview
item.description: “Of course there is concern," Ambassador to the United Arab Emirates Yossi Shelley told The Jerusalem Post, adding that the incident showed the strength of the Abraham Accords.

item.title: One person injured, one killed after light aircraft crashes in northern Israel
item.description: Israel's Fire and Rescue Authority announced that firefighters from the Hadera station had arrived at the scene and were working to extinguish a fire which had broken out and was spreading.

item.title: IDF: 170 Hamas, PIJ terrorists killed in Gaza were misrepresented as 'innocent journalists'
item.description: The journalists' identities and terrorist affiliations were verified using documents released by the terrorist organizations themselves and materials recovered by IDF troops during Gaza operations.

item.title: IDF gives rejection of 'NAZA' film claims, disputes civilian death ratios, AI targeting abuse
item.description: The intelligence interviewees were not experts, but rather a middle step of the targeting process, who knew much less about the final step • Guardian: 24 interviewees in film taken from pool of 100

item.title: Gaps narrow between coalition, opposition blocs as security is spotlighted in public agenda - poll
item.description: According to the poll, the coalition bloc gained two seats this week, rising to 51, while the Zionist opposition bloc fell by two seats to 53.
